info.title: Octa Pass sync API
info.description: Stores and syncs end-to-end encrypted vaults. The server only ever sees ciphertext. Binary values are base64url without padding; errors are application/problem+json.

post.summary:
A new device and session made from this one, for a program on the same computer that the
signed-in app vouches for (the CLI, plan 05): no password, no second step, because the session
asking already passed both. It keeps this session's SSO age, appears in the device list as a
device of its own (signed out like any other), and the owner gets the new sign-in email.

204.description: The device was signed out and its live connections got session-revoked. Deleting the current device is a sign-out.

AccountBundle.description:
The encrypted account keys and public keys. Nothing in it is readable by
the server except the email, KDF parameters, salt and public keys.

accountId.description: Present in responses, ignored in requests.

oneOf.description:
The account's signed key record. Set by `POST /v1/transparency/publish`, ignored in
sign-up requests.

recoveryWrappedAsk.description: Ciphertext envelope: the ASK sealed by the recovery code.

wrappedAsk.description: Ciphertext envelope: the Account Symmetric Key sealed by the Account Unlock Key.

wrappedPqPrivateKey.description:
Ciphertext envelope: the ML-KEM-768 seed sealed by the ASK. Set by `POST
/v1/transparency/publish`, ignored in sign-up requests.

wrappedPrivateKeys.description: Ciphertext envelope: the account private keys sealed by the ASK.

AccountLookupResponse.description: `GET /v1/accounts/lookup?email=`: what a client needs to seal a key to an account.

fingerprint.description: Six groups of four digits, for display. Clients should compute their own from the keys.

oneOf.description:
The account's signed key record, which carries its ML-KEM key. Absent until one of the
account's devices publishes it.

AttachmentRecord.description:
An encrypted file kept with an item. Its name, type, size and key are in the
item's encrypted details; the server knows only the stored size.

size.description: Stored (encrypted) bytes, as counted against the quota.

oneOf.description:
`put`: omit to create, a revision to update, `"*"` to update whatever is
stored. `delete`: required, a revision or `"*"`. `restore`: ignored.
Required for `put`, ignored otherwise.

operations.description: At most 1,000, each item at most once.

BatchResult.description: The outcome of one operation, in request order.

oneOf.description: Set when the operation failed.

status.description: The HTTP status the single-item endpoint would have answered.

BreachEmailRequest.description: `POST /v1/health/breach-email`. In the body so the address stays out of URLs and logs.

registrationUpload.description: base64url OPAQUE `RegistrationUpload` for the new master password.

oneOf.description: First message on a connection, and again after every token refresh.

ClientMessage.description: A message from the client on `GET /v1/ws`.

ConnectEventsRequest.description: `POST /v1/security-log/connect`: what Octa Pass Connect handed out, one blob per secret.

sealedDetails.description:
Envelopes sealed under the account key, at most 100 in one request. The server can't read
them. Each holds the time it happened, so a late upload still says when.

sealedKey.description: The ASK, or the vault key, sealed to the contact (context `emergency:…`).

vault.description: The shared Family vault, created with the family.

name.description: Plaintext metadata, visible to the server. At most 64 characters.
Plaintext metadata, visible to the server. At most 64 characters.
For telling tokens apart, at most 64 characters.

CreateServiceAccountRequest.description:
`POST /v1/vaults/{vaultId}/service-accounts`. Everything was made on the creator's device; the
token isn't here.

encryptedName.description: The name, sealed so that only the creator can read it.

expiresAt.description: RFC 3339. Left out, it lasts until it's revoked.

grant.description: `recipientAccountId` is the service account's id. Role `read` or `write`.

keyId.description: base64url id of the vault key the grant seals.

ciphertext.description: The encrypted item snapshot. Its key stays in the link's `#` fragment.

expiresAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp, 1 hour to 30 days from now.

passphraseRequired.description: Whether the viewer also needs the access passphrase (the ciphertext says so too).

CreateVaultRequest.description: `POST /v1/vaults`: a shared vault and the owner's own grant.

grant.description: Role `owner`, to the signed-in account, by the signed-in account.

keyId.description: base64url key id (16 bytes) of the vault key.

CreatedScimToken.description: A new SCIM token. `secret` is shown once: the server keeps only its hash.

CredentialsUpdate.description:
The password-dependent part of the account bundle, as a master password change or reset
replaces it. The ASK itself stays the same, so nothing else is re-encrypted.

accountSalt.description: base64url, 16 bytes. A new one with every change.

recoveryWrappedAsk.description:
Ciphertext envelope: the ASK sealed by a new recovery code. Required by a reset, which
always replaces the recovery code; optional for a change.

wrappedAsk.description: Ciphertext envelope: the ASK sealed by the new Account Unlock Key.

confirmEmail.description: Must equal the account email (compared after trimming and lowercasing).

DeletedItem.description: A permanently removed item. Kept for 90 days so other devices learn about it.

name.description: Shown to the user in their device list. At most 64 characters.

DeviceRecord.description: A signed-in device, as listed by `GET /v1/devices`.

current.description: Whether this is the device making the request.

lastSeenAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp. Updated on token refresh and WebSocket sign-in.

EmailBreach.description: A breach, from Have I Been Pwned.

keyStale.description:
A vault scope only: the vault's key was rotated, so the sealed key opens nothing new until
the grantor renews it with `PUT /v1/emergency-contacts/{id}/key`.

organiserRecovery.description: The family's organiser holds this record: `takeover` access, and no reading.

releasesAt.description: When a pending request releases the key unless the grantor denies it.

received.description: Accounts that chose this account as their contact.

oneOf.description:
Account scope only: the grantor's bundle, whose private keys the released ASK opens.
A vault scope gets nothing that could open the grantor's other vaults.
The grantor's account key, and with it every vault the grantor can open.
One vault the grantor owns.

EmergencyScope.description: What the emergency contact gets once access is released.

EmergencyTakeoverRequest.description:
`POST /v1/emergency-contacts/{id}/takeover`, with the `X-Reauth-Token` header of the contact's
own account (purpose `emergency-takeover`). See plan 06, "Takeover design".

account.description: `recoveryWrappedAsk` is required: a takeover always replaces the recovery code.

registrationUpload.description: base64url OPAQUE `RegistrationUpload` for the grantor's new master password.

signature.description:
base64url Ed25519 signature by the grantor's signing key over
`"openpass/v1/emergency-takeover" ‖ 0x00 ‖` length-prefixed `recordId, grantorId,
contactId, currentAccountSalt, registrationUpload, accountSalt, wrappedAsk,
recoveryWrappedAsk`.

FamiliesResponse.description: `GET /v1/families`: the family the account belongs to, and invitations to others.

FamilyInvite.description: An invitation that hasn't been accepted yet.

invites.description: Pending invites. Only the organiser sees them.

maxMembers.description: Members plus pending invites can't go over this.

Grant.description:
A member's sealed and signed copy of a vault key, made on the granter's device. The server
checks its shape and who may grant what, but can't open it or check the signature's meaning.

wrappedVaultKey.description: The vault key sealed to the recipient: 105 bytes, base64url.

IfMatch.description: The precondition on a batch operation: a revision, or `"*"` for any revision.

grant.description: For the account `GET /v1/accounts/lookup` returned for that email.

keyId.description:
base64url key id of the vault key the grant seals. When given, a key rotated since
fails with `vault-key-changed`, so no grant of an old key is stored.

ItemKeyUpdate.description: An item's re-wrapped item key, in a key rotation.

deletedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp. Set while the item is in the trash.

revision.description: The vault revision of the item's last change.

ItemRevision.description:
One past version of an item, as it was before an edit. Opened with the item's current key: an
edit keeps the key, and rotating the vault key only re-wraps it.

revision.description: The vault revision this version was written at.

updatedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp: when this version was written.

KdfParams.description: Password KDF parameters, stored per account so they can be raised later.

frontier.description: The perfect subtrees covering every leaf before `start`, largest first, base64url.

KeyLogEntry.description: A label's latest record and its audit path.

inclusion.description: RFC 9162 audit path to `head`, base64url hashes.

consistency.description: RFC 9162 consistency proof from the size in `since` to this head, base64url hashes.

oneOf.description: Absent until a quorum of witnesses has cosigned a checkpoint.
Absent when the log has no witnesses.

KeyLogIdentity.description: The log's public keys, which clients pin.

oprfKey.description: base64url ristretto255 element: the VOPRF public key behind labels.

signKey.description: base64url Ed25519 public key that signs heads.

oneOf.description: Absent when nothing is logged under the label.

KeyLogWitnessPolicy.description: The witnesses a key log sends its checkpoints to (plan 03, "Witnesses").

quorum.description: How many of them must have cosigned.

KeyLogWitnessed.description: The newest checkpoint a quorum of witnesses cosigned.

checkpoint.description: A C2SP checkpoint as a signed note: the log's signature, then the witnesses'.

consistency.description: RFC 9162 consistency proof from the checkpoint's size to `head`, base64url hashes.

KeyRecord.description:
What an account says about its own public keys, signed by its Ed25519 key. Its hash is what
the key log holds. See `docs/developers/sync-api.md`, "Key log".

label.description: base64url label of the account's email (32 bytes).

logId.description: base64url id of the log this record is for.

LinkDeviceRequest.description:
`POST /v1/devices/link`: a session of its own for another program on this device that the
signed-in app vouches for (the CLI, plan 05). The answer is a sign-in's
([`LoginFinishResponse`]).

device.description: The new device, as the device list shows it.

trustedDeviceToken.description: From an earlier sign-in on this device. A valid one skips two-step sign-in.

Keep it with the session and send it on the next sign-in from this device, so that sign-in
skips the second step. Replaces any token sent with the login. It works only while this
device is still in the account's device list (not signed out, session not lapsed), for at
most 30 days.

loginId.description: Opaque handle for `login/finish`, valid for 30 seconds.

MaskedEmailAlias.description: One address on the server's masked email service.

blocked.description: Messages refused: blocked senders and failed sender checks.

forwarded.description: Messages forwarded to the account's email.

paused.description:
The service stopped forwarding after bounces or spam reports. Setting `enabled` to true
starts it again.

replied.description: Replies sent out through the alias.

MemberRecord.description: A vault member, with the public keys other members seal to and verify against.

fingerprint.description:
Six groups of four digits. Clients compute it themselves from the keys: a server could
lie about both.

grantedBy.description: Absent for a personal vault's owner, who holds no grant.

oneOf.description:
The member's signed key record, which carries their ML-KEM key. Absent until one of the
member's devices publishes it.

wrappedVaultKey.description: Ciphertext envelope: the vault key sealed by the ASK.

OrgEvent.description: An entry in the admin activity log.

actor.description: The email of who did it, unless that account is gone.

subject.description: What it was done to: an email, a group's name or a vault id.

type.description: A stable kebab-case name, for example `member-removed`.

OrgInvitation.description: An invitation the signed-in account received. `policies` are what joining agrees to.

OrgInviteRecord.description: A pending invite, as admins see it.

OrgInviteRequest.description: `POST /v1/orgs/{orgId}/invites`. The answer is the same whether or not the email has an account.

role.description: `member` or `admin`. Owners are made from members, by an owner.

OrgMemberRecord.description: A member, as admins see them.

ssoLinked.description: Whether this member has signed in through the identity provider.

OrgPendingGrant.description:
Someone a vault's key should be sealed to. This list comes from the server, so a client shows
it to a person, with a fingerprint it computes itself, before sealing anything.

oneOf.description:
The account's signed key record, which carries their ML-KEM key, so the grant can be
hybrid and checked against the key log. Absent until one of their devices publishes it.

upgrade.description: Replaces a grant with a lower role.

OrgPolicies.description: An organisation's rules for its members. A policy restricts; it never moves a key.

disableEmergencyAccess.description:
Enforced by the server: members can't add emergency contacts, and existing contacts don't
reach organisation vaults.

disableExport.description: Applied by clients: exports leave out organisation vaults. A modified client can ignore it.

disableShareLinks.description: Enforced by the server: members can't create share links.

maxAutoLockMinutes.description: Applied by clients: the longest auto-lock a member may choose, in minutes.

minPasswordLength.description: Applied by clients when a master password is set. The server never sees the password.

requireSso.description:
Enforced by the server: members sign in through the identity provider after their master
password. Owners are exempt, so a broken provider can't lock the organisation out.

requireTwoStep.description:
Enforced by the server: organisation vaults are withheld from a member without two-step
sign-in, who also can't turn it off.

ssoMaxAgeHours.description: How many hours a sign-in with SSO lasts, 1 to 8760; 0 checks only at sign-in.

OrgRecord.description: The signed-in member's view of their organisation.

accessWithheld.description: Whether this member is breaking a policy, so organisation vaults are withheld.

OrgRole.description:
What a member can do in an organisation. Roles live on the server and open nothing: vault keys
reach people only through grants.

OrgSamlCertificate.description: A signing certificate an organisation pinned for SAML.

notAfter.description: When the certificate says it expires. Only its key is used, so this is for the admin.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the DER, colon-separated hex, as identity providers show it.

OrgSamlRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/orgs/{orgId}/sso/saml`: the identity provider's metadata, or its three fields. Saving
replaces OpenID Connect settings, if any, and needs a new test sign-in.

certificates.description:
Without metadata: its signing certificates, PEM or base64 DER, 1 to 4 (more than one while
it rolls its key over).

entityId.description: Without metadata: the IdP's entity id.

metadataXml.description: The IdP's metadata XML (`EntityDescriptor`). It isn't fetched from a URL: paste it.

ssoUrl.description: Without metadata: its HTTP-Redirect single sign-on URL.

OrgSamlServiceProvider.description: This server as a SAML service provider for one organisation.

metadataUrl.description: The SP metadata, for providers that import it.

baseUrl.description: The SCIM 2.0 base URL to give the identity provider.

OrgScimTokenRecord.description: A SCIM bearer token, without the token.

createdBy.description: The email of the owner who made it, unless that account is gone.

OrgSsoRecord.description: `GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/sso`. The client secret never comes back.

callbackUrl.description: The redirect URI to register at the provider.

oneOf.description:
Which protocol the saved settings use; absent when there are none. `issuer` and
`clientId` are OpenID Connect's; `saml` is SAML's.

samlServiceProvider.description: What to register at a SAML identity provider, whatever is saved now.

testedAt.description: When a test sign-in last finished with these settings. `requireSso` needs one.

clientSecret.description:
Sealed under the server secret. Leave out for a public client, or to keep the stored one
when only the other fields change.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer URL. Its discovery document is fetched and checked.

OrgVaultAccessPlan.description: What a vault is waiting for from a key holder.

canApply.description:
Whether the signed-in account holds this vault's key and may manage it. When false, the
lists say what's waiting, and a vault manager has to apply it.

keyId.description: base64url id of the current vault key; send it back with the grants.

rotate.description: The key should be rotated: someone lost access.

OrgVaultGrantsRequest.description:
`POST /v1/orgs/{orgId}/vaults/{vaultId}/grants`: grants made on the key holder's device after a
person reviewed them. Each must match what the organisation entitles.

keyId.description: base64url key id of the vault key the grants seal.

OrgVaultGroup.description: A group's access to a vault.

OrgVaultRecord.description:
An organisation vault, as admins see it. Its name is encrypted in the vault, so an admin who
isn't a member sees only the id.

managerCount.description: Members who can grant access and rotate the key. At 0 nobody can, and it can only be deleted.

oneOf.description: The signed-in account's role, if it's a member.

rotationPending.description: Someone lost access and the key hasn't been rotated yet.

OrganiserRecoveryRequest.description:
`POST /v1/families/{familyId}/organiser-recovery`: a member lets the family's organiser help
recover their account. The server takes the rest from the family.

sealedKey.description: The member's ASK sealed to the organiser (context `emergency:<member>:<organiser>:ask`).

PasswordRegistrationRequest.description:
`POST /v1/account/password/registration` and `POST /v1/auth/recover/registration`: the OPAQUE
registration for the new master password. Nothing is stored.

recoveryId.description: Only for `recover/registration`: the reset it belongs to.

accountSalt.description: base64url, 16 bytes. Unknown emails get a deterministic fake salt.

oneOf.description: Only on `conflict`: the item as currently stored on the server.
Only on `second-factor-required`.
Only on `sso-required`.

wrappedPqPrivateKey.description: Ciphertext envelope: the ML-KEM-768 seed sealed by the ASK.

PushPlatform.description: Which service delivers a phone's pushes.

PushTokenRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/devices/current/push`: where this device can be woken up. A push names no account,
vault or item; it says only `sync` or `alert`.

sandbox.description: APNs only: a development build, reached through Apple's sandbox.

token.description: At most 4096 characters: hex for APNs; letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `:` for FCM.

details.description: Ciphertext envelope of the item details.

encryptedItemKey.description: Ciphertext envelope: the item key sealed by the vault key.

overview.description: Ciphertext envelope of the item overview.

skipHistory.description:
The write is bookkeeping, not an edit (a one-time code's counter moving): the version it
replaces isn't added to the item's history.

reauthToken.description: Send as the `X-Reauth-Token` header. Single use.

ReauthPurpose.description: What a reauth token may be used for. Each token works for one purpose, once.

ReauthStartRequest.description: `POST /v1/auth/reauth/start`: a fresh OPAQUE login by a signed-in user.

RecoverFinishRequest.description:
`POST /v1/auth/recover/finish`. The account's sessions all end; sign in with the new master
password afterwards (with the second step, if two-step sign-in is on).

registrationUpload.description: base64url OPAQUE `RegistrationUpload` for the new master password.

signature.description:
base64url Ed25519 signature by the account's signing key over
`"openpass/v1/account-recovery" ‖ 0x00` and then, each as a u32 big-endian length and its
UTF-8 bytes: accountId, challenge, registrationUpload, accountSalt, wrappedAsk,
recoveryWrappedAsk. Proves the device opened the account key.

RecoverStartRequest.description:
`POST /v1/auth/recover/start`: a master password reset with the recovery code begins with a
code sent to the account's email.

devVerificationCode.description: Only present when the server runs in dev mode.

recoveryId.description: Names this reset in the next calls. Returned whether or not the email has an account.

account.description: The account bundle: the recovery code unwraps its `recoveryWrappedAsk` on the device.

refreshToken.description: The previous refresh token stops working. Presenting it again revokes the session.

trustedDeviceToken.description:
No longer sent: a device is trusted only from its own sign-in. Kept so older clients and
servers still understand each other.

devVerificationCode.description: Only present when the server runs in dev mode.

RenewEmergencyKeyRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/emergency-contacts/{id}/key`: the grantor seals a vault's current key to the contact
again, after a rotation.

keyId.description:
base64url key id of the vault key it seals. A key rotated since fails with
`vault-key-changed`.

sealedKey.description: The vault key sealed to the contact (context `emergency:…:vault:…`).

RotateVaultRequest.description: `POST /v1/vaults/{vaultId}/rotate`: a new vault key, in one transaction.

grants.description: Exactly one per current member, with the member's current role.

invites.description:
Family vaults: a grant of the new key for each pending invite to keep, with the
invite's role. Pending invites left out are cancelled, so none keeps the old key.

items.description: Every item in the vault, trash included, wrapped under the new key.

keyId.description: base64url key id of the new vault key.

revision.description: The vault revision the client synced to. Anything newer fails with `vault-changed`.

serviceGrants.description:
A grant of the new key for each active service account (`recipientAccountId` is its id,
with its role). One left out can no longer read the vault and needs a new token.

wrappedVaultKey.description: A personal vault only, which has no grants: the new key wrapped by the account key.

challengeId.description: For `login/second-factor`. Single use, valid for `expiresIn` seconds.

oneOf.description: Present when `methods` includes `webauthn`.

SecondFactorMethod.description: A way to finish two-step sign-in.

recoveryCode.description: Spaces, dashes and case don't matter.

SecurityEvent.description: An entry in the account's own security log.

deviceName.description: `vault-exported`: the device's name and platform when it exported, kept after it signs out.

exportAttachments.description: Whether the file holds the vault's attachments (only the encrypted export does).

otherAccountEmail.description: The other account involved, while it exists.

sealedDetail.description: `connect-secret-read`: an envelope only the account can open.

serviceAccountId.description: The `service-account-*` entries: which one. Its name is in the service account's record.

SecurityKeyRecord.description: A security key or passkey registered for two-step sign-in.

lastUsedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last sign-in with it.

emailBreachChecks.description: An HIBP key is set, so `POST /v1/health/breach-email` answers.

maskedEmailRelay.description:
This server has its own masked email service: the routes under `/v1/masked-email` work.
Absent on older servers.

pushRelay.description:
Phones can register for pushes (`PUT /v1/devices/current/push`): the server is set up with
a push relay and registered with it.

oneOf.description: The access token was accepted. Send a new `auth` before it expires.

A vault the account can access changed. Sync it if `revision` is newer
than the one you have.

Members of a vault were added or removed, or its key was rotated. Sync: a vault that is
gone from the sync response is one this account can no longer access.
The account was deleted. Wipe local data; the server closes the connection.
This device was signed out. The server closes the connection.

ServerMessage.description: A message from the server on `GET /v1/ws`. Never carries item data.

challenge.description: base64url, single use, good for a minute.

ServiceAccountRecord.description: A service account, as `GET /v1/vaults/{vaultId}/service-accounts` lists it.

grantedBy.description:
The account that signed its current grant. When that isn't `createdBy`, the token can't
verify the grant and a new one is needed.

signature.description: base64url Ed25519 signature over the auth message (plan 03).

ShareLinkRecord.description: One of the signed-in account's share links, without its ciphertext.

viewsLeft.description: After this view. At 0 the link is already gone.

SignupMode.description: Whether new accounts can be created on a server.

challengeId.description: For `login/sso`. Keep it on the device: it isn't the same as the browser URL.

url.description: Open in a browser. The provider's page, then a page showing a 6-digit code.

code.description: The 6-digit code the browser page showed.

SsoProtocol.description:
The protocol of an organisation's SSO step. Either way it runs after the master password and
decides only whether the sign-in may go on.

hasMore.description:
The response stopped at a page limit. Store the vault revisions and
sync again with them as `since`.

items.description: Items changed after the requested revision, including items in the trash.

vaults.description: Every vault the account can access, with its current revision.

code.description: The current code from the authenticator app.

recoveryCodes.description: Only when this turned two-step sign-in on: shown once, never retrievable again.

TotpSetupResponse.description: `POST /v1/account/two-step/totp`: a new authenticator secret, not active until confirmed.

secret.description: Base32 (RFC 4648, no padding), for typing into an authenticator app.

enabled.description: Whether signing in on a new device asks for a second step.

methods.description: Empty when two-step sign-in is off.

rpId.description: The WebAuthn relying party id security keys are registered for.

UsageResponse.description:
`GET /v1/account/usage`: what the vaults the account owns hold (trash
included), and the server's limits. Shared vaults count against their owners.

maxFileBytes.description: The largest single attachment, as stored (encrypted).

VaultExportedRequest.description:
`POST /v1/security-log/exports`: what a client sends once the user saved an export. Nothing
from the vault, only the format and whether the attachments went with it.

VaultGrant.description:
The signature half of a grant. With the vault id, this account's id, `role` and
`wrappedVaultKey` from the `VaultRecord`, it is the whole signed grant.

granterPublicSignKey.description:
base64url Ed25519 public key of the granter, as it was when they signed. Compare its
fingerprint out of band before trusting it.

oneOf.description:
Shared and family vaults: the rest of this account's signed grant. Verify it against
`granterPublicSignKey` before using the vault key.

keyId.description:
Shared and family vaults: base64url key id of the current vault key. Item writes whose
`encryptedItemKey` was wrapped under another key are refused with `vault-key-changed`.

orgId.description: The organisation this shared vault belongs to. It opens like any shared vault.

revision.description:
Increases by one on every change to the vault's items. In a sync
response it's the revision the response is complete up to: the
current one unless `hasMore` is set.

wrappedVaultKey.description:
Personal vaults: the vault key sealed by the ASK. Shared and family vaults: the key sealed
to this account's X25519 key, as signed in `grant`.

VaultRole.description:
What a member may do. Each role includes the ones below it: `read` views, `write` also
edits items, `manage` also adds and removes members and rotates the key, `owner` also grants
and removes owners. A vault is deleted with its last owner.

WebAuthnAssertion.description: A WebAuthn assertion (`AuthenticatorAssertionResponse`), binary values as base64url.

WebAuthnCreationOptions.description:
WebAuthn `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions`, binary values as base64url. Attestation is
`none`; ES256 (-7) and Ed25519 (-8) keys are accepted.

algorithms.description: COSE algorithm ids, in order of preference.

excludeCredentials.description: Credential ids already registered, so the same key isn't added twice.

WebAuthnRequestOptions.description: WebAuthn `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` for the second step, binary values as base64url.

allowCredentials.description: Credential ids of the account's security keys.

userVerification.description: `discouraged`: the password already ran, the key only proves possession.

id.description: base64url, random per account (not the account id).

bearer.description: Opaque access token, valid for 15 minutes
